growth.note: The bound applies to every fixture measured at more than one size, and it is 1.25 because the cost per plan entry has to stay flat as the fleet grows: `fleet` grows the number of entries and keeps each entry's own work constant, `mesh` grows one entry's work with the fleet and keeps the plan linear in it, and a quarter of slack absorbs constant-factor noise without admitting any super-linear term.

worked.note: Moved by open-the-repository-to-a-consumer: the library records the identity of the package set whose platform definitions elaborated it, so `lib/default.nix` takes one more argument and exports one more value. The cost is a constant per evaluation rather than per entry, which is why every figure here moved by a fraction of a percent and the largest fixture moved least: gc.totalBytes of `worked` rose 5.8 per entry of 43562, and envs.bytes 0.7 of 8884, while values.number, sets.bytes and list.elements fell by about as much.
